Statute No. 01 of 2016 of Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council
Statute on Pinnawala Iperanigama Theme Park Establishment

The statute to establish a theme park with related trust board and matters connected there with orincidents thereto, which is for display the economic, social and educational glory of a traditionalvillage of Sabaragamuwa Province.
Be it enacted by the Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council of the Democratic Socialist Republic of SriLanka
1)1.1 This statute may be cited as the “Pinnawala Iperanigama Theme Park Statute No. 01
of 2016 and shall come into operation on the date of its approval by the Governor.
1.2 There shall be established an Trust Board for Pinnawala Iperanigama Theme Park
(Hereinafter referred as Theme Park) and the members of the trust board shall beconsider as persons mentioned in Section No. 04.
1.3 Pinnawala Iperanigama Theme Park shall be an unit, which implemented by the Chief
Ministry of Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council and shall has perpetual succection anda common seal.
1.4 Hereinafter “Minister” shall referred as the Chief Minister of Sabaragamuwa Province.
1.5 Hereinafter “Trust Board” shall referred as The Trust Board of the Pinnawala
Iperanigama Theme Park.
1.6 Hereinafter “Account” shall referred as the account related to Pinnawala Theme Park.
1.7 Hereinafter “Governor” shall referred as The Governor of Sabaragamuwa Province.
1.8 Hereinafter “Secretary” shall referred as the Secretary of the Chief Ministry of
Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council.
2)2.1 Demonstrate live models related with the heritage and the economic, social and cultural
glory of a traditional village of Sabaragamuwa Province, which has a chronicle frompre historic era to future generation.
2.2 Provide the opportunities to study the structure of a traditional village with its live
models and equipments used there as far off days, to students of year 5 scholarshipexam, GCE (O/L), (A/L) and higher education.
2.3 Demonstrate economic system of a traditional village for local and foreign tourists.
2.4 Conserve the features and traditional equipment for the future generation.
2.5 Promote the tourism in Sabaragamuwa Province.
2.6 Generate direct and indirect employment opportunities
2.7 Create a tourists attraction and generate foreign exchange.
Short Title and thedate of operation

2.9 Provide a marketing space for artistic creations of the traditional artists of
Sabaragamuwa Province.
2.10 Provide opportunities to perform dancing skills of traditional dancers of Sabaragamuwa
Province.
2.11 Organize seminars, programs and field visits for protect the heritage.
2.12 Execute as an income generation system for provincial fund.
3)3.1 Theme park should be contained by the features to demonstrate a traditional village of
the Sabaragamuwa Province, Sri Lanka.
3.2 Indigenous doctor’s house (Weda Gedara), Village Headman’s House (Arachchila

Gedara), Traditional Coffee Bar (Kopi Kade) Black Smith’s Shop (Kammala),Carpenter’s Shed (Wadu Maduwa), Handloon Weaver’s Place (Athyanthra RedipiliGedara), Potter’s House (Kumbal Gedara), Head Former’s House (Maha GamaralageGedara), Tank (Wewa), Chena (Hena), Traditional Fence (Dandu Weta), Hut on Tree,Paddy Field, Threshing floor (Kamatha), Traditional Rice Granary (Wee Bissa),Buddhist Temple, Open Theatre, Drum Makers House, Teacher’s House, Laundres’sHouse, Theme Park’s Restaurent, Entrance and Front Office, Exit Building and souvenirshop are to be consider as the features of Theme Park.
3.3 The Trust Board shall has the power to add additional features compatible with the
objective of the Theme Park.
4)4.1 The Trust Board consists as follows :
Chief Advisor-Chief Minister of Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council
Conceptual Advisor -Chief Secretary, Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council.
President of the Trust Board - Secretary, Chief Ministry of Provincial Council
Members of the Trust Board

- Two representatives of the Chief Minister- Secretary, Sabaragamuwa Provincial Education Ministry- Secretary, Sabaragamuwa Provincial Tourism Ministry- Secretary, Sabaragamuwa Provincial Industrial Ministry- Secretary, Sabaragamuwa Provincial Agricultural Ministry- Deputy Chief Secretary (Planning)- Deputy Chief Secretary (Financial Management)- Deputy Chief Secretary (Administrative)- Deputy Chief Secretary (Engineering Services)- Deputy Chief Secretary (Personnal and Training)- Director (Planning), Provincial Chief Ministry- A representative of the Chief Secretary
The Trust Board consists of 13 members as above

All the members of Trust Board should be appointed by the Minister
5)5.1 The term of office of the trust board is 03 years. At the end of the period of three
years, the minister should appoint the members again.
5.2 Functions of the Trust Board should be as follows .
(a) The Trust board should be hold meetings more than once a month or twice and
should get the relevant managerial decisions.
(b) The Trust Board shall have the power to recruit, promote, provide disciplinary
rules, terminate the service on disciplinary matters and recruit employees undercontract/casual/substitute basis.
(c) The Trust Board shall have the power to determine the salary scales of all
employees under contract/casual/substitute basis.
(d) The Trust Board shall be the disciplinary authority of all employees.
(e) Service extension power on contract basis employees shall be a power of the
Trust Board.
(f) The trust board shall have the power to add additional features to make the Theme
Park a more reliable model traditional village for local and foreign tourists.
(g) Participatory allowance for the trust board members shall be decided by the Trust
Board under the approval of The Minister.
(h) Determination of the incentives for foreign tourist agencies and tourists guides
to promote introducing tourists to the Theme Park shall be a power of the TrustBoard.
(i) The Trust Board shall have the power to identify and implement the necessary
actions to promote the Theme Park and gain the attraction of local and foreigntourists.
(j) The Trust Board shall determine the opening hours of the Theme Park and the
working hours of employees.
6)6.1 The secretary of the chief ministry of Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council shall act as
the Chairman of the Trust Board. He shall act as the Chair Person, the chief and themain policy maker of the Trust Board.
6.2 The Trust board can give him an acting allowance of 1/3 of his current salary to perform
the duties as the Chairman of The Trust board.
7)7.1 Chief Executive Officer of the Theme Park shall act as the secretary of the Trust Board.
Keeping the minutes of the Trust board is a duty of him.
8)8.1 When the chairman is absent, members of the Trust Board has the power to appoint
another member among them as the acting chairman as the day meeting.

9)9.1 Total number of the Trust Board is 13 members. Quorum for the meeting shall be
consider as 07 members.
10) 10.1 The Minister receives following powers :-
a) Power of calling special meeting sessions at his discretion.
b) Power of appointment and removal on members of the Trust Board
c) In case of exposure of an undisciplined activity or a corruption of a member, the
minister has the power to remove them from the Trust Board.
d) Power of obtain the bank account and financial information of the Trust Board.
11) 11.1 Member of the parliament, member of a provincial council or a mayor/chairman of a
local authority, is disqualified from being appointed or acted as a member of the TrustBoard.
11.2 A person declared to be an offender by a court of Sri Lanka should not be appointed or
acted as member of the Trust Board.
12) 12.1 The Minister has the power to appoint new member in case of a resigning or death of a
representative of the Minister, he has the power to appoint a new representative to theTrust Board to settle the vacancy for the left period of the time.
12.2 The Chief Secretary of the Provincial Council has the power to appoint new member in
case of a resigning or death of the representative of Chief Secretary, he has the powerto appoint a new representative to the Trust Board to settle the vacancy for the leftperiod of the time.
12.3 In case of retirement, transfer, promotion, resigning or death of a member of rest
ones, the minister should appoint the successor of the related designation as a memberof the Trust Board.
13) 13.1 If resigns a member who represents the Chief Minister of the Chief Secretary of the
Provincial Council, he may aware the Chief Minister, Chief Secretary and the Chairmanof the Trust Board within a calendar month.
14) 14.1 The Trust Board should maintain a separate bank account named “Pinnawala Iperanigama
Theme Park” is a state bank.
14.2 The Provisions of Part 3 of the Provincial Council’s Act, No. 42 of 1987, shall apply
to the financial control of the authority.
14.3 The following receipts shall be subjected to the account of “ Pinnawala Iperanigama
Theme Park”
(A) Cash and donations by Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council Fund.
(B) Earnings of the Theme Park.
(C) Cash and donations by a Government Ministry/a Department or another institute.

15.2 The Trust Board shall have the capability and power to pay any purchase, award, gift or

15.3 The Trust Board shall have the power to sell, mortgage or lease some property of the

16.3 The Trust Board shall maintain the account properly in relation to income, expenditure,
assets, liabilities and other purposes of the Theme Park.
16.4 Auditing of the account should be done in accordance with the provisions of the Article
154 of the constitution, for auditing a accounts of a state corporation.
16.5 The audit report shall lay before the Trust Board on following meeting after it received.
17) 17.1 The cheques should sign by the Chairman of the Trust Board or Chief Executive Officer
with Finance Assistant or Manager.
18) 18.1 Appointment the Chief Executive Officer.
(a) An officer of a all island service shall appoint as the Chief Executive Officer of

the Theme Park, under instructions on the Minister. This appointment shall bedone by the secretary under the agreement of the Trust Board and under theapproval of Minister. The Trust Board has an ability to pay an acting allowance of1/3 of his current salary.
or
(b) When not appointed as above the Minister can appoint full time Chief Executive
Officer. The Trust Board shall determine the salary and allowances under theapproval of Minister.
(c) The Trust Board shall identify required qualifications to appoint the Chief
Executive Officer.
(d) Roles of the Chief Executive Officer are continuing the general administration,
financial administration, staff administration and maintaining the Theme Park asa profitable institution under the Chief Ministry.

18.3 The Trust Board has the power to appoint workes under casual/substitute/contract basis
due to necessity in addition to above mentioned staff.
18.4 The Trust Board has the power to extent the service period of casual/substitute/contract
basis staff appointed for certain tasks.
18.5 The Trust Board shall recruit casual/substitute/contract basis staff as permanent staff
after the service period of one year.
(a) Under this, only workers who qualified with a performance potential should
recruited to the permanent staff.
(b) The Trust Board has the ability to extent the time of service of contract basis
workers.
(c) After recruit as permanent staff the workers are paid salaries, living cost
allowances and the Trust Board shall pay related payments to the EmployeesProvident Fund (EPF) and Employees Trust Fund (ETF).
(d) Prepare salary scales for the staff, prepare a promtion system, staff training and
decision making on disciplinary control shall be done by the Trust Board.
(e) The Trust Board has the power to revise the number of employments and number
of the positions on service necesstity.
(f) The Trust Board has the power to determine the duties of employees.
(g) All officers and employees of the Theme Park established under this statute shall
be considered as provincial public servants.
(h) All employees must be subject to Establishments Code, Financial Regulations,
Sabaragamuwa Provincial Financial Rules, Statutes, Circulars and regulationsenacted from time to time.
(i) The Trust Board receives the power to load any loss or damage done by any officer
or employee in good faith or without intention.

20) 20.1 Theme Park included as Open Theatre.
(a) The Trust Board shall identify an art institute for perform traditional dancing/
drama in the Open Theatre for a identified time period.
(b) When identifying as art institute the Trust Board shall give first priority to art
institute’s in Rambukkana, second priority for art institute’s in Kegalle districtand third priority for art institute’s in Ratnapura district.
(c) The Trust Board shall pay a partial payment for the art institute, from their
performance income from Open Theatre. The Trust Board shall determine thepercentage and the amount to be charged from local and foreign tourists.
(d) The Trust Board shall educate students and local and foreign tourists about Sri
Lankan traditional rituals, offerings, dancing and dramas.
(e) The Trust Board shall identify a certain time period for perfome these events.
(f) The trust board can identify art institutes and artists, determine their contract
period and their participatory allowance.
21) 21.1 The Trust Board can determine the daily rental or fare on giving Open theatre for hire
basis. The Trust Board can given the Open Theatre on hire basis for Drama and programsbased on indigenous values.
22) 22.1 The Trust Board shall give the exhibition stalls near the exit door to state and private
sector institutions under an identified proper method.
22.2 Exhibition stalls shall be used to sell Theme Park identical artistic items, creations of
artists in Sabaragamuwa Province and to introduce nationally important artisticcreations to local and foreign tourists.
22.3 It shall not allow selling or introducing artificial or non-traditional items in these
exhibition stalls.
22.4 The Trust Board shall determine the rental for the exhibition stalls.
23) 23.1 The Trust Board shall charge an identified fare from professional photographers and
